trigger.stage: strict post-harvest analysis after the snapshot guest manifest, harvested raw CSV, and Linux restoration had all passed
trigger.cause: One duplicated UART transport summary was truncated to throughput_msg_s=9.6 while the second complete copy reported 9.607. Both retained every required field, so the analyzer correctly detected conflicting complete records before deriving the same metrics from verified raw samples.

invalidated_observation.interpretation: All primary protocol and raw-data gates completed, but this attempt remains excluded because its then-current analyzer returned failure. A read-only replay with the corrected analyzer passed and was used only as regression evidence, not as a campaign result.

regression_first.pre_fix: test_raw_samples_replace_conflicting_uart_metric_summaries failed with conflicting complete IVC-CONTROLLER-TRANSPORT records

post_fix.targeted_conflict_tests: PASS with verified raw; PASS rejection without raw
post_fix.cargo_clippy: not applicable because no Rust crate was modified

evidence_contract: When no raw CSV is supplied, conflicting complete UART metric records remain a hard failure.

When a raw CSV has passed snapshot guest-manifest, harvest, byte-hash, schema, sample-count, sequence, timestamp, actuator, and control-error checks, conflicting duplicate UART metric summaries are treated as transport damage and that metric family is derived from raw rows.
A unique UART metric summary is still cross-checked against raw-derived values; a mismatch remains a hard failure.
Controller outcome and reliability counts, RTOS counts and sequences, result hashes, and lifecycle markers remain strict and are never replaced by this fallback.
